title: NHL Picks & Predictions Today - Best NHL Bets by Odds Shark

picks.analysis: Draisaitl to score is in play to +100 because he's scored the third-most goals in the NHL over the past three years, and the Canucks allowed the most goals per 60 minutes and sixth-most expected goals per 60 last year. Additionally, I particularly value No. 29 projecting to jump the board with superstar Connor McDavid at five-on-five in the season opener because the duo have been on the ice for a monster 7.69 goals per 60 minutes over the past two years.

Podkolzin is set up to succeed with a top-line gig jumping the boards with superstars Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, and the Canucks allowed the most goals per 60 minutes and sixth-most expected goals per 60 last year, too. So, with the McDavid-Draisaitl duo being on the ice for 7.69 goals per 60 minutes over the past two years, I like the Russian winger to find the scoresheet against his former team in the season opener down to -115.

This Under 6.5 is in play to -110 because the Oilers are commited to improved defense and allowed just 0.91 goals per 60 minutes while surrendering the eighth-fewest high-danger scoring chances per 60 at five-on-five during the preseason. Edmonton was already a possession monster with a fifth-ranked Corsi For percentage at five-on-five across the past three years, and Vancouver scored the fewest goals per 60 minutes while generating the fifth-fewest expected goals per 60 at 5-on-5 last season.
I’d back Leon Draisaitl to find the back of the net to 54%.

The preseason is a mess, with guys who have played more than 100 games in their careers allowed to play in only two preseason games. This is going to lead to some sloppy early hockey, and that puts the value on the dogs — and no one is bigger than Vancouver. The Oilers were the same price against Vancouver last year near the end of the season, when Edmonton was playing its best hockey. There are worries about Tristan Jarry in net for Edmonton, as he is not even an average NHL goalie. There is also a system change with the home team, as new head coach Mike Babcock and his extra luggage are now in charge behind the bench. This is a young Vancouver team that might be in better shape for Game No. 1 than a veteran-heavy Edmonton squad, and these 3x MLs are very appetizing this week.

picks.analysis: Edmonton has topped Vancouver in seven of their past nine meetings, and the Oilers are going to be improved on defense with Mike Babcock behind the bench. Edmonton was already a possession monster with a fifth-ranked Corsi For percentage at five-on-five across the past three years, and the Oilers also ranked second in expected goals percentage to reinforce their consistent ability to tilt the ice in their favor. Turning to Podkolzin, he's set to jump the boards with superstars Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, and the go-to duo have been on the ice for a monster 7.69 goals per 60 minutes over the past two years.

Play up to 42%. Jack Eichel remains one of Vegas’ premier scoring threats after netting 27 goals last season. At home, he generated 72 individual scoring chances and 25 high-danger opportunities at five-on-five. Against a Chicago defense that struggled to suppress offense, Eichel should get several quality looks.

Play up to 58%. Patrick Kane should have a major offensive role with Connor Bedard sidelined. He produced 57 points in 67 games last season and is expected to skate on Chicago’s top line while also working on PP1. That usage gives the veteran multiple paths to record a point in the opener.

Play up to 52%. Vegas has a clear talent edge at home against a Chicago team opening the season without Connor Bedard. The Blackhawks ranked near the bottom of the NHL in both scoring and goals allowed last year, while Vegas posted a +24 goal differential at T-Mobile Arena. A multi-goal win is very realistic.

Connor Bedard is out, but there is still plenty of young scoring in this Chicago lineup against a Vegas team that is likely not strong in net with Carter Hart and may not be as motivated after a long Stanley Cup Final run that ended in the middle of June. The Hawks have legit scoring rookies on both of their top lines in Anton Frondell and Roman Kantserov. Frondell has a terrifying shot after seeing it at the World Juniors and World Hockey Championships, where he scored six goals in 11 games. He is 4.3x to score and is a look for sure. The exciting one, and one that might be flying under the radar, is Kantserov, who is playing on the top line and PP1. He scored 36 goals in 63 games in the KHL last year at age 21 and has shorter odds to win the Calder than Frondell, who already has 12 NHL games under his belt at 19 years old. The value on opening night is with the dogs.

picks.analysis: This combo fits the expected game script. Chicago struggled defensively last season, while Vegas has enough firepower to do most of the scoring itself. Jack Eichel also averaged 3.91 shots per game at home, giving his 3.5 SOG leg a strong foundation in a favorable matchup.

Colorado holds a huge home-ice advantage in the altitude at Ball Arena, and in particular, the Avalanche’s speed will be a nightmare for the Kings. Colorado paced the NHL in speed bursts over 20 mph per game, while Los Angeles ranked 17th, after all. Additionally, the Kings allowed the third most expected goals per 60 minutes at five-on-five during exhibition play. Of course, the Avs also went 26-9-6 at home with a second-ranked 58.0 Corsi For percentage at five-on-five last year.
